name: How long does detached ADU construction take after permits are issued?

mainEntity.name: How long does detached ADU construction usually take once the permit is approved and the crew starts work?
mainEntity.text: How long does detached ADU construction usually take once the permit is approved and the crew starts work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once the permit is issued, the construction phase typically becomes the next major timeline driver. A detached ADU can move relatively quickly on a flat, uncomplicated site, but the schedule expands when the project includes new foundations, trenching, utility upgrades, retaining walls, or premium finishes. The framing and shell may go up quickly, yet inspections, mechanical work, and finish selections can add weeks. The most reliable way to predict timing is to ask for a construction schedule broken into phases: mobilization, foundation, framing, rough trades, drywall, finishes, inspections, and final turnover. Homeowners should also ask how long utility coordination may take, because that is often outside the builder’s direct control. Delays are common when decisions are made late, materials are backordered, or inspection dates are not scheduled promptly. A realistic timeline is a project-specific schedule, not a generic promise of a few months.
acceptedAnswer.description: After permits are issued, detached ADU construction commonly takes several months, with the exact timeline depending on size, foundation type, utility work, inspections, and finish level. Custom units and sites with access or utility challenges usually take longer than straightforward builds.
